key_insight: Wall heat losses strongly alter early flame propagation in confined channels, promoting tulip flame formation and later distortion compared with adiabatic-wall behavior.
engineering_relevance: For safety-critical combustion systems and narrow ducts, accounting for conjugate heat transfer and geometry is essential to predict flame acceleration, shape inversion, and near-wall dynamics.
method: Direct numerical simulation of the fully compressible reactive Navier–Stokes equations
Detailed chemistry and transport for stoichiometric hydrogen–air flames
Conjugate heat transfer with conductive channel walls and external convective/radiative losses
evidence_signal: The simulations were compared against adiabatic-wall cases and were reported to reproduce the main experimentally observed features of tulip flame dynamics.
watch_item: Results depend on detailed chemistry, transport, and wall heat-transfer modeling, so quantitative predictions may be sensitive to boundary-condition and material-property assumptions.
paper_title: The Effect of Heat Loss During the Early Stages of Flame Propagation and Tulip Flame Formation
